analysis.title: GS Bartlett - GS TMT TODAY 10.19.26
key_insights: Futures point to a recovery day (Nasdaq +100bps, S&P +40bps, Russell +50bps) after a difficult week for risk. GS's AI bellwether basket GSTMTAIP finished -11.5%, its 2nd worst week since ChatGPT was released in Nov 2022.

Prime Services reported the largest net selling in 8 weeks, mostly in Info Tech, Semis and Semicap Equipment. Semis net selling as a % of gross market value was the largest on record. Mutual funds sold heavily across Tech and AI infrastructure, with dollars rotating largely outside TMT.

GS upgrades CoreWeave (CRWV) to Buy from Neutral (Borges) with 73% upside to a $106 price target (down from $139). The stock is down 43% since the Aug 11 2Q EPS and 24% in 5 trading days, on credit market volatility and debate over frontier vs off-frontier demand. Borges expects near-term contract economics datapoints to be more positive than the market expects.

GS argues CoreWeave's enterprise value tracks the spread between its unlevered IRR and WACC. It thinks investors underestimate the upward revisions to unlevered IRR and overestimate the upward revisions to WACC.

Musk said he will give one SpaceX share to every kid in America next year. About 72 million US children at the $146 share price is roughly $10.5B. The mechanics are unclear. SPCX reports earnings Tuesday.
Apple's $1,999 iPhone Duo folding phone saw shipping estimates slip into January within minutes of Friday preorders, which points to short supply and strong demand ahead of the Oct 23 release.

GS PB: Info Tech saw its largest % de-grossing in 2 months and its largest % net selling on record (since 2016), with long sales to short sales at 4.7 to 1. All major regions were net sold, led by EM Asia and North America. Semis and Semi Equip led in dollars.

The Prime book is now underweight Info Tech vs MSCI World by -8.4% (23rd percentile vs the past year, 29th vs five years). Gross/Net allocation to Info Tech is 21.3%/23.5% (48th percentile vs the past year, 90th vs five years).

GS raises its global server TAM by 31% in 2027E and 45% in 2028E. General server value rises 17%/11% and AI server shipments are raised, citing better mix and higher memory costs that drive cloud service provider spending.

GS AI server forecasts imply AI chip demand of 18m/29m/38m units in 2026-28E and about 60%/50% ASIC penetration in 2028E (global / global-tier). GS sees an AI infrastructure upcycle across CSP capex, fabless shipments and foundry capacity.

Callahan: NDX closed Friday on its lows, back below its 50/100-day moving averages and through trend-line support, down about 550bps on the week. That is its largest weekly drop since Liberation Day, led by Semis down about 11.5%.
Callahan attributes the repricing of growth expectations to rates/oil tensions and a debate on the linearity of the AI build-out. GIR estimates AI capex contributes about half of S&P 500 EPS growth.

Unlike July's momentum unwind, which felt technical, the current episode has investors debating which overhang is most acute: earnings, elections, rates/credit, ROIC, inflation, product momentum, build-out execution or policy.

Macro this morning: E-minis +60bps, Nasdaq futures +1.2%, US 10-year yield stable at 5.07%, crude -1%. Nvidia's Jensen Huang said he expects the turmoil to pass and AWS's CFO said AI spending is sustainable. Premarket SMH +2.5%, DRAM +4.5%, CRWV +2%.
14% of SPX market cap reports this week, including META and TSLA on Wednesday. Fed members are in blackout. NAHB Housing Market Index is due at 10am.

China activity data was mostly better: GDP 4.5% vs consensus 4.4%, industrial production 5.5% vs 5.4%, retail sales 1.1% vs 0.5%. Europe is lower (FTSE -90bps, DAX -1.1%, CAC -1.3%), with France lagging after weekend riots.

Prime: US L/S net leverage fell 3.2 pts, the largest weekly decline since Liberation Day, to 43.7% (0th percentile over 5 years). 8 of 11 sectors were net sold. Healthcare, Comm Svcs and Staples were net bought, which points to a more defensive posture.

Semis fell 8 consecutive sessions, the longest streak since May 2006, with memory at the center (MU and SNDK lower in 7 of 8 sessions). The S&P 500 fell 1.9% on the week. Oil, Retail and Bond Proxies outperformed, while NeoClouds, Optical Networks and Memory underperformed.

CTA/trend followers are expected to buy some government bond futures in the baseline scenario. They are short about $164mm/bp DV01 globally, with a further $20mm of covering expected over one week and $64mm over one month. In equities, GS expects $18bn of buying over one week and $30bn over one month, led by Europe and more neutral in the US, after $55bn of global selling in the past month.

Derivatives: QQQ closed lower five sessions in a row, but the vol market did not fully react until Friday afternoon. VIX spiked to its highest level since July and VVIX jumped 17 pts, one of the largest 1-day moves in four years. Asset managers entered Friday with VIX futures positioning at the shortest on record.
Levered ETFs took in over $8bn over four days, the largest weekly inflow in GS's dataset. Levered and inverse ETFs hold $176bn AUM and $444bn gross exposure.

GS Baskets: likes buying SPXXAI (ex-AI basket) as the conditions that justified AI concentration show cracks. Preferred option structures are AI Hardware protection, Broad AI protection and an ex-AI upside call spread.

TMT specialists: SOX is down 8 straight sessions, the HF VIP TMT Basket is -13% since 10/8 and the GS TMT Mo' pair is -14% in 3 days. Focus is on whether positive AI earnings get rewarded and can arrest negative momentum.

GS US Weekly Kickstart: the Cyclicals vs Defensives pair fell 6% in two weeks. GS expects S&P 500 EPS growth of 29% in 2026 and 18% in 2027 (adjusted for accounting distortions). 53% of S&P 500 firms have beaten Q3 EPS so far, vs a 50% long-term average and 64% over the past four quarters. Revision breadth is declining.
TTWO 2FQ27 earnings preview: GS reiterates the company is well positioned heading into the holidays and the GTA VI release on November 19.

Street actions: Upgrades to CRWV (Buy, GS), DDOG (Outperform, Bernstein), GLBE (Overweight, Morgan Stanley), GPN (Overweight, KeyBanc), INTC (Neutral, JPMorgan). Downgrade: PINS (Buy, Phillip Securities).

Earnings calendar: Tue 10/20 Pre: 3M, EFX, GM, Hasbro, MSCI, VICR; Post: NFLX, PEGA, United Airlines, SPCX. Wed 10/21 Pre: AT&T, MCO; Post: CCI, IBM, LRCX, META, ROL, TSLA, TXN, United Rentals. Thu 10/22 Pre: Blackstone, CMCSA, DOV, HON, INFY, Nokia, ROP, SPOT, TTMI; Post: BE, KN, MXL, RNG, RHI, SSNC, VRSN, WDC. Fri 10/23 Pre: AmEx.

vol_and_positioning: VIX spiked on Friday to its highest level since July after VIX futures were aggressively bought. VVIX jumped 17 pts, one of the largest 1-day moves in four years. Front-month VIX outperformed its beta to SPX by 1.5 vols, the largest outperformance since April.
Asset managers entered Friday with VIX futures positioning at the shortest level on record.
US L/S net leverage fell 3.2 pts to 43.7% (0th percentile over 5 years), the largest weekly decline since Liberation Day.
Info Tech saw the largest % de-grossing in 2 months and the largest % net selling on GS Prime record (since 2016), long sales to short sales 4.7 to 1.
Levered ETF inflows exceeded $8bn over four days, the largest weekly inflow in GS's dataset. Levered and inverse ETFs hold $176bn AUM and $444bn gross exposure.
Hedge funds and asset managers were better sellers, with supply in Macro Products and Tech.
CTAs are short about $164mm/bp DV01 in global government bonds. GS baseline expects $18bn of equity buying over one week and $30bn over one month, after $55bn of global selling in the past month.
geopolitical: Escalating Ukraine/Russia tensions: Ukraine escalated attacks on Russian energy infrastructure, and Trump waived new sanctions on Russia while continuing to criticize Ukraine.
Wide-spread protests and riots in France over the weekend weighed on French equities.

tension_points.bull_case: Jensen Huang expects the turmoil to pass and AWS's CFO said AI spending is sustainable. GS raises its server TAM by 31%/45% in 2027/28E and sees an AI infrastructure upcycle. Levered ETF inflows seek to find the bottom, and the AI complex is bouncing premarket (SMH +2.5%).
tension_points.bear_case: The AI basket had its 2nd worst week since Nov 2022, semis fell 8 straight sessions, and Info Tech saw record net selling. Credit stress, a debate on the linearity of the AI build-out, and AI capex contributing half of S&P EPS growth raise the stakes. GS says conditions that justified AI concentration show meaningful cracks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Whether positive earnings prints in the AI complex are rewarded with share price gains and arrest negative momentum, as the TMT specialists frame it for earnings season.

tension_points.bull_case: Borges expects near-term contract economics datapoints to be more positive than the market expects, and thinks investors underestimate upward revisions to unlevered IRR.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit market volatility raises questions on whether and at what rate CoreWeave can finance its next phase of growth, and investors may be overestimating the fall in token monetization at its customers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Upward revisions to WACC larger than the upward revisions to uIRR would narrow the spread GS ties to enterprise value.
